title: MailerLite Pricing: Every Plan Compared (2026)
summary: MailerLite pricing includes a free tier with limits and paid plans above it. Compare subscriber caps, features, and costs to pick the right plan.
body_markdown:
## Connect MailerLite to your other tools with Activepieces


You can use Activepieces, a workflow tool with an MIT-licensed core and a MailerLite integration, to move contacts from your other tools into MailerLite, but it's optional and doesn't change what MailerLite charges.


Your bill still follows subscriber count, so a workflow that adds more people to your list raises the price like any other signup.


### What MailerLite already automates natively


Check what MailerLite does by itself before adding anything. It has built-in integrations with other services and an API for anything you build yourself.


That covers many setups: a signup form on your site, a connected store, or a developer who can call the API directly. Each of these adds no second tool to maintain and no second system to pay for.


If your contacts already arrive through one of them, stop here, because anything more is another moving part with no benefit.


Confirm which integrations your plan includes on MailerLite's own pricing and integrations pages, since availability can differ by plan and changes over time.


### Where a separate workflow tool adds something


When your contacts originate in several systems and none of the native routes covers all of them, a workflow tool earns its place.


Activepieces lets you build one workflow that takes a record from any of those sources and sends it into a MailerLite subscriber list, so you maintain one connection rather than several separate ones.


The MailerLite integration is one of the 746 in the` packages/pieces/community` directory of the[open-source monorepo on GitHub](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/tree/main/packages/pieces/community) , where the count comes from the folders themselves and roughly 60% of them are community-contributed; the core is MIT-licensed.


On Activepieces a run is 1 credit however many steps it has, so the filtering steps described next don't add to the credit count.


Read the diagram as a consolidation point: four sources, one place where you decide what reaches your list and in what form.


That single point is also where you can apply your own rules, such as which records should become subscribers at all.


Since every contact you sync counts toward your list size, filtering before the write is the one lever that keeps the workflow from inflating your bill.


Whether the effort is worth it depends on how many sources you have. With one source, native tools are simpler.


With several, the Activepieces side is cheap to test: the free plan is $0 with unlimited flows and 1,000 credits a month, and Plus is $20 a month for 10,000 credits.


Both run on Activepieces Cloud or on your own servers, and its[pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) is the authority on current figures.
